items.scope: Dugite native v2.53.0-4: Git, Git LFS, Git Credential Manager and platform libraries/tools
items.action: Implemented: every release target now ships a corresponding-source archive built in CI (scripts/release/native-source.cjs, policy third_party/native-source.json) holding the pinned upstream sources of the exact bundled Git, Git LFS and Git Credential Manager (all platforms) plus, for Windows, the Git for Windows fork and the MSYS2/MinGW package sources, build-extra and OpenSSL. The archive is staged, checksummed, attested and required by the publication gate. Disclosed deviations: bash uses the MSYS2 5.2.037-2 source package (the -1 source is no longer hosted); OpenSSL 3.5.5 comes from the upstream tarball plus the Git for Windows packaging commits; MinGit's package-versions.txt is stale versus git.exe 2.53.0.windows.4. Remaining step: after the final release commit, run the release matrix, review the archives, then record the reviewer, date and per-target input hashes and mark this item cleared. Review of the 5c6977f Windows inventory matched Bash and both OpenSSL DLLs to Git for Windows SDK revisions 7dcc4cda92934c4d306c4958304581f23a2ca31a and d8562a834b61d0111c21a6510788bbedf358719b respectively. The Windows GCM payload included Microsoft NativeInterop 0.20.6. The maintainer selected GCM removal on all targets. Verify the new candidate has no GCM private files, retains authentication and includes the required native sources.

items.scope: Native Codex and TypeScript-Go embedded dependencies
items.action: Per-platform findings are recorded for macOS, Linux and Windows x64 (third_party/evidence/native-ai-platform-packages.json, from the published npm tarballs, not run on those platforms). TypeScript native 7.0.2: NOTICE.txt and LICENSE are in every platform package and byte-identical. Codex 0.162.1: every platform package also ships an optional voice runtime (LGPL-2.1 GStreamer/GLib, Opus, libffi, PCRE2, and Microsoft vcruntime140.dll on Windows) that FDO does not use; it is excluded from the app by webpack.main.config.js and enforced by third_party/distribution-policy.json (codex-voice-runtime), and the Codex CLI was confirmed to run without it. Linux ships a bubblewrap helper (LGPL-2.0-or-later) whose vendored source is added to the Linux native-source archive (openai/codex at commit 092d3acd). Still open: Codex helper binaries (rg, zsh, Windows sandbox executables) and Rust crates rely on the upstream NOTICE and the source-lock inventory; no complete native SBOM exists. After the final release commit, review the packaged builds, then record the reviewer, date and per-target input hashes. On 2026-11-20 the maintainer chose to retain bundled Codex and hold publication until its redistribution evidence is complete. The pinned supplier ripgrep manifest identifies 15.2.0. The production workflow pins codex-zsh-v0.1.0 manifest c534eab89dcea7e3d8a5e5b3f49c025c7c64cd4e4d9814ee24871de58a9359a1. Linux zsh and Linux/Windows ripgrep match the supplier executables exactly. Both macOS architectures match after removing signatures on comparison copies and normalizing the __LINKEDIT virtual-size field. The alpha manifest comparison did not represent production. The candidate adds the upstream zsh and ripgrep notices. Review their inclusion and the remaining embedded dependencies before clearance.
